section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section discusses the order of Torah and mitzvos in the two paragraphs of Shema, and the precise language used for Torah study in each.
section.t: "And you shall teach them to your children and speak of them,"
and afterwards it is stated, "And you shall bind them as a sign upon your hand, etc.,"
the mitzvah of tefillin,
about which our sages, of blessed memory, said,
"The entire Torah is equated to tefillin,"
the intention of which is regarding the mitzvos of the Torah,
and this means,
that the verse precedes the matter of Torah to the matter of mitzvos.
And it is known the precise observation of our Nesi'im,
that in the second paragraph of Shema it is stated,
"And you shall bind them as a sign upon your hand, etc., and you shall teach them to your children, etc.,"
that this verse is in reverse order,
preceding the matter of mitzvos
(the mitzvah of tefillin)
to the matter of Torah.
Also, one must understand what is the reason that the order where Torah precedes mitzvos is specifically in the first paragraph of Shema,
and the order where mitzvos precede Torah is specifically in the second paragraph of Shema.
Also, one must understand the precise language regarding the matter of Torah,
that in the first paragraph it is stated, "And you shall sharpen them, etc.,"
according to Rashi's explanation
(from the midrashim of our sages, of blessed memory),
that it is an expression of sharpening,
that they should be sharp in your mouth, so that if a person asks you something
(a halachah)
you will not need to stammer over it, but rather tell him immediately
(and only afterwards is it stated, "and speak of them"),
whereas in the second paragraph it is stated, "And you shall teach them, etc.,"
which this term includes all modes of study
(even if the study is not in a manner of being sharp in your mouth, etc.).
